title: Make the raw fader value type consistent
problem: Volume::SetFadervalue accepts a float but immediately passes it to Helper::Fadervalue2dBfs(uint16_t), silently truncating fractions and exposing a misleading API for the console's 12-bit raw fader value.
reproduce: Inspect the declaration and definition of Volume::SetFadervalue at the pinned revision: both accept float while the only conversion helper and hardware callback accept uint16_t.
acceptance: The Volume setter, conversion helper, and physical fader path use one explicit uint16_t raw-value type, with no implicit float-to-integer conversion at the setter boundary.
repair: Change Volume::SetFadervalue's declaration and definition to uint16_t, matching the 0..4095 physical fader domain and the existing helper contract.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the API mismatch on the pinned baseline and the consistent raw fader type after the repair. The repository's full build requires external libraries and Linux headers; GitHub's target builds remain authoritative.
verification.ownerCheck: Build the X32/M32 target, move a physical fader through its range, and confirm the surface still reports and recalls positions from 0 through 4095 without jumps.

selection.reason: The issue is unassigned, has no related PR, identifies an exact two-line type mismatch, and the intended raw fader domain is established by the hardware callback and conversion helper.

publish.commitMessage: fix: use raw integer type for fader values

upstream.suiteOutputIncludes: PASS: raw fader type contract is consistent
